name: Azariah
overview: Azariah, a male figure noted as the son of Obed, played a supportive role in the reign of King Joash of Judah. His identity is primarily defined by this unique relationship and his involvement in the political-religious landscape of Judah. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Azariah means 'YHWH has helped,' reflecting a recognition of divine assistance. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 23:1, is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological implication consistent with Hebrew naming traditions.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Azariah as the son of Obed, establishing a clear paternal link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the available records.
scriptureSignificance: Azariah's significance lies in his support of Joash as king of Judah, a role that situates him within the critical period of Judah's monarchy. His connection to Obed and his involvement in the political-religious affairs underscore the interplay between faithful leadership and divine providence. Although the prior reference to Azariah as Uzziah highlights themes of prosperity and the dangers of pride, this particular Azariah's contribution centers on his allegiance during Joash's reign, illustrating the importance of faithful support in God's governance of His people.
